content.title: Mechanical and Plumbing Permits
content.summary: Mechanical work associated with a building permit, including tenant improvements, is permitted as part of a Combined Building Permit. Separate mechanical and plumbing permits are not required when applying for a Combined Building Permit. Over the Counter permits are available for certain single-family fixture replacements without plan review.

steps.title: Apply for Combined Building Permit
steps.text: All mechanical work associated with a building permit (including tenant improvements) is permitted as a component of the building permit (referred to as Combined Building Permit). Separate mechanical and plumbing permits are not required when a Combined Building Permit is applied for. If you are a subcontractor, contact the general contractor or project manager to verify the proper plans were reviewed and approved for your portion of the work.

steps.title: Request Mechanical and Plumbing Inspections
steps.text: Mechanical and plumbing inspections may be requested through the Permit Portal.

steps.title: Apply for Over the Counter Permit
steps.text: When a plan review is not required, you can apply online through the permit portal to have a permit issued immediately. Over the Counter issuance of mechanical and plumbing permits are available for replacement of single family fixture installations including water heaters and appliances.

steps.title: Submit Plan Set for Mechanical Rooftop Units
steps.text: Mechanical rooftop units require plan review. Submit a plan set that includes: cover sheet with vicinity map, rooftop plan showing location of units and screening, screening details, curb and connection details.

steps.title: Submit Supplemental Documents for Mechanical Rooftop Units
steps.text: Submit equipment cut sheets. For equipment weighing over 400 pounds, provide structural calculations for over-turning, sliding and gravity.
